correctness.rationale: The logarithmic moment kernels concentrate asymptotically on disjoint annuli. The induced step-symbol map is identity plus a compact operator on ell-infinity, forcing the radial moment range to be closed and finite-codimensional. The preadjoint from ell-one to L-one is injective by an entire-function moment argument; closed-range duality and Hahn--Banach then force surjectivity. Finite-dimensional Fredholm splittings give a bounded linear right inverse. Bdarneh's homogeneous decomposition then identifies this with exact realization of every U(n)-intertwiner.

originality.rationale: The inspected 2026 preprint proves only strong-operator density in general and, for the logarithmic weight, one non-square-root-uniformly-continuous eigenvalue sequence. Searches did not locate bounded-symbol surjectivity or a bounded linear lifting. Grudsky--Vasilevski 2002 can prescribe arbitrary bounded eigenvalues only in a larger symbol class whose symbols are unbounded in general, while classical bounded radial symbols remain restricted by the Esmeral--Maximenko square-root-uniform-continuity theorem.

value.rationale: The result shows that the recent failure of the classical metric description is maximal: for this logarithmic weight every bounded spectral sequence is realized by one bounded radial Toeplitz symbol. It upgrades strong-operator density to exact equality with the full U(n)-commutant and provides continuous linear symbol selection.

disclaimer: Not independent validation, peer review, formal verification, or a guarantee of first discovery.
